content: 1. Mnemonic for Airway, Breathing, and Circulation (ABC): This mnemonic is used to prioritize the assessment and management of critically ill patients. It emphasizes the importance of first ensuring a patent airway, followed by adequate breathing, and then circulation. 2. APGAR Score: The APGAR score is a backronym used to evaluate the health of newborns immediately after birth. It stands for Appearance (skin color), Pulse (heart rate), Grimace (reflex irritability), Activity (muscle tone), and Respiration (breathing effort). 3. ASHICE: This mnemonic is used in emergency medicine to gather key patient information: Age, Sex, History, Injuries/Illness, Condition, and Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) or additional information. 4. FAST (Face, Arms, Speech, Time): This is a stroke recognition tool. It highlights the need to assess facial drooping, arm weakness, and speech difficulties, and to act quickly (time is critical). 5. H’s and T’s: These are the reversible causes of cardiac arrest. The H’s include Hypoxia, Hypovolemia, Hydrogen ion (acidosis), Hypo-/Hyperkalemia, and Hypothermia. The T’s include Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade (cardiac), Toxins, Thrombosis (coronary or pulmonary). 6. Is Path Warm? This mnemonic identifies suicide risk factors: Ideation, Substance abuse, Purposelessness, Anxiety, Trapped feelings, Hopelessness, Withdrawal, Anger, Recklessness, and Mood changes. 7. OPQRST: This is a symptom evaluation checklist: Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region/Radiation, Severity, and Time. 8. RICE (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation): This is a standard treatment protocol for sprains and bruises to reduce swelling and promote healing. 9. SOCRATES for Pain Assessment: This mnemonic evaluates pain characteristics: Site, Onset, Character, Radiation, Associated symptoms, Timing, Exacerbating/Relieving factors, and Severity. 10. SOAP Notes: A structured method for documenting medical records: Subjective (patient-reported symptoms), Objective (clinical findings), Assessment (diagnosis), and Plan (treatment strategy). 11. SLUDGE: This mnemonic describes the symptoms of cholinergic crisis: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, Gastrointestinal upset, and Emesis. 12. Afferent vs. Efferent Connections: Afferent connections arrive at a structure (sensory input), while efferent connections exit a structure (motor output). 13. Anterior Leg Muscles Mnemonic: The Hospitals Are Not Dirty Places helps recall the structures: Tibialis anterior, extensor Hallucis longus, anterior tibial Artery, deep fibular Nerve, extensor Digitorum longus, and Peroneus tertius. 14. Brachial Plexus Posterior Cord Branches: Mnemonics like STAR (Subscapular, Thoracodorsal, Axillary, Radial) and RATS (Radial, Axillary, Thoracodorsal, Subscapular) help recall the branches. 15. Lateral Cord Branches: Mnemonics such as Lucy Loves Me (Lateral pectoral, Lateral root of the Median nerve, Musculocutaneous nerve) aid in memorization. 16. Medial Cord Branches: Most Medical Men Use Morphine (Medial pectoral, Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm, Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm, Ulnar nerve, Medial root of the Median nerve) is a helpful mnemonic. 17. Bowel Components: The sequence from proximal to distal is Duodenum, Jejunum, Ileum, Appendix, Colon, Sigmoid, and Rectum. 18. Carotid Sheath Contents: I See 10 CC’s in the IV represents the Internal Carotid artery, Cranial Nerve 10 (Vagus), Common Carotid artery, and Internal Jugular Vein. 19. Cavernous Sinus Contents: OTOM CAT describes the lateral wall components (Oculomotor nerve, Trochlear nerve, Ophthalmic nerve, Maxillary nerve) and the sinus contents (Carotid artery, Abducens nerve). 20. Coeliac Trunk Branches: Left Hand Side refers to the Left gastric artery, Hepatic artery, and Splenic artery. 21. Mnemonic for the Tarsal Tunnel Contents: Tom, Dick, and Harry or Tom, Dick (and very nervous) Harry represents the Tibialis posterior, flexor Digitorum longus, flexor Hallucis longus, artery, vein, and nerve. 22. Mnemonic for Cranial Nerves: Oh, Oh, Oh, To Touch And Feel Very Good Velvet, AH. represents the cranial nerves in order: Olfactory, Optic, Oculomotor, Trochlear, Trigeminal, Abducens, Facial, Vestibulocochlear, Glossopharyngeal, Vagus, Accessory, and Hypoglossal. 23. Mnemonic for Cranial Nerve Functions: Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More indicates whether each cranial nerve is Sensory (S), Motor (M), or Both (B). 24. Mnemonic for Extraocular Muscle Innervation: LR6 SO4 R3 indicates that the Lateral Rectus is innervated by Cranial Nerve VI, the Superior Oblique by Cranial Nerve IV, and the remaining muscles by Cranial Nerve III. 25. Mnemonic for the Layers of the Retina: A mnemonic for the retinal layers is In New Generation It’s Only Optic Nerves, representing the layers from outermost to innermost. 26. Mnemonic for the Path of Sperm: My Boyfriend’s Name is STEVE represents the Seminiferous tubules, Epididymis, Vas deferens, Ejaculatory duct. 27. Mnemonic for the Sternal Angle: RAT PLANT represents Rib 2, Aortic arch, Tracheal bifurcation, Pulmonary trunk, Ligamentum arteriosum, Azygos vein, Nerves (cardiac and pulmonary plexuses), and Thoracic duct. 28. Mnemonic for the Vertebral Column: Breakfast at 7, Lunch at 12, Dinner at 5 represents the 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, and 5 lumbar vertebrae. 29. Mnemonic for Carpal Bones: Some Lovers Try Positions That They Can’t Handle represents the Scaphoid, Lunate, Triquetrum, Pisiform, Trapezium, Trapezoid, Capitate, and Hamate bones. 30. Mnemonic for the Causes of Aortic Regurgitation: CREAM represents Congenital, Rheumatic damage, Endocarditis, Aortic dissection/root dilation, and Marfan’s syndrome. 31. Mnemonic for Aortic Stenosis Symptoms: SAD represents Syncope, Angina, and Dyspnea. 32. Mnemonic for the Heart Valves: Try Pulling My Aorta represents the Tricuspid, Pulmonary, Mitral, and Aortic valves. 33. Mnemonic for the Management of Myocardial Infarction: BOOMAR represents Bed rest, Oxygen, Opiates, Monitor, Anticoagulate, and Reduce clot size. 34. Mnemonic for the Treatment of Ventricular Tachycardia: LAMB represents Lidocaine, Amiodarone, Mexiletine/Magnesium, and Beta-blockers. 35. Mnemonic for White Blood Cell Types: Never Let Monkeys Eat Bananas represents Neutrophils, Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Eosinophils, and Basophils.
